definition_en: a particular way of doing, making, or expressing something
core_image: 同一种动作，落在纸上却有各自的笔迹
scene: 这位画家有自己独特的风格。The painter has a style of her own.
sceneCN: 这里 style 是「风格」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这位画家有自己独特的风格。

senses.title: Artistic manner
senses.definition: a particular way an artist or writer expresses ideas
senses.definitionCN: 艺术家或作家表达思想的独特方式
senses.example: The painter has a style of her own.
senses.exampleCN: 这位画家有自己独特的风格。
senses.why: This is the core sense in art.
senses.whyCN: 这是艺术领域的核心义项。

senses.title: Design
senses.definition: the design or shape of clothes or objects
senses.definitionCN: 衣服或物品的设计或样式
senses.example: She likes the style of that coat.
senses.exampleCN: 她喜欢那件外套的款式。
senses.why: Design borrows the idea of a manner.
senses.whyCN: 设计借用了「方式」这一概念。

senses.title: Way of acting
senses.definition: a way of behaving or working
senses.definitionCN: 行为或工作的方式
senses.example: His style is to listen first.
senses.exampleCN: 他的作风是先听别人说。
senses.why: A person's manner becomes a style.
senses.whyCN: 一个人的处事方式也成了作风。

intro.en: Style first named a pointed tool for writing.
intro.cn: style 最初指书写用的尖笔。

items.en: Stilus was a pointed writing tool.
Style named a manner of writing.
Style entered English as a way with words.
items.cn: style 作为用词方式进入英语。

items.en: Style widened to art and design.
items.cn: style 扩展到艺术与设计。

items.en: Style also named a way of living.

note.en: Style is compared with look-alike words and with words for manner.
note.cn: 把 style 与形近词以及表示方式的词作比较。

entries.definition: a popular way of dressing or behaving
the shape or plan of something

normalIntro.en: Style is the fingerprint of a way of doing something.
normalIntro.cn: style 是做事方式留下的指纹。

normal.en: The painter has a style of her own.
normal.cn: 这位画家有自己独特的风格。

normal.en: She likes the style of that coat.
normal.cn: 她喜欢那件外套的款式。

normal.en: His style is to listen first.
normal.cn: 他的作风是先听别人说。

normal.en: The letter was written in a formal style.
normal.cn: 这封信是用正式风格写的。

normal.en: That song is out of style now.

abstract.en: Style is what remains when the rules are forgotten.
abstract.cn: 规则被忘掉之后，留下的就是风格。

abstract.en: A style can be copied, but not the hand behind it.
abstract.cn: 风格可以被模仿，背后的那只手却不能。

abstract.en: Every age writes in its own style and calls it natural.
abstract.cn: 每个时代都用自己的风格书写，并称之为自然。

examples.en: The painter has a style of her own.
examples.cn: 这位画家有自己独特的风格。

examples.en: She likes the style of that coat.
examples.cn: 她喜欢那件外套的款式。

examples.en: His style is to listen first.
examples.cn: 他的作风是先听别人说。

dict_mnemonic.text: style 是「风格、款式、作风」；in style 是时髦地，out of style 是过时，writing style 是写作风格，style guide 是体例指南。

root: 来自拉丁语 stilus（书写用的尖笔），经古法语进入英语；由笔和笔迹，引申为写作与艺术表达的方式，再扩展为服装款式、做事作风和生活方式。

sensesIntro.en: Style is an artistic manner, a design, or a way of acting.
sensesIntro.cn: style 是艺术风格、设计款式，或行为作风。

core.en: The personal mark left on a common task.
core.cn: 在共同的事情上留下的个人印记。

branches.en: The painter has a style of her own.
branches.cn: 这位画家有自己独特的风格。

branches.en: She likes the style of that coat.
branches.cn: 她喜欢那件外套的款式。

branches.en: His style is to listen first.
branches.cn: 他的作风是先听别人说。

branches.en: Art and conduct both reveal a personal manner.
branches.cn: 艺术和为人，都显露出个人的方式。

branches.en: A coat and a habit can share the same style.
branches.cn: 一件外套和一种习惯，可以有同一种风格。

intro.en: Style builds adjectives and nouns with -ish, -ist, and -istic.
intro.cn: style 借助 -ish、-ist 和 -istic 构成形容词和名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base stilus named a writing tool.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词 stilus 指书写工具。

items.example: The two styles are very different.
The room is styled like a studio.
items.exampleCN: 这房间布置得像工作室。
他穿了一件时髦的外套。

latinEntries.example: Stilus gave English style.
latinEntries.exampleCN: stilus 演变为英语的 style。

definition_en: the topic being discussed, a course of study, a person studied, or being affected by something
core_image: 被放在讨论中央、供人观看与研究的那个东西
scene: 今天这节课的主题是天气。The subject of today's lesson is the weather.
sceneCN: 这里 subject 是「主题」（第 1 个义项）；句意：今天这节课的主题是天气。

senses.title: Topic
senses.definition: the thing being discussed or written about
senses.definitionCN: 正在被讨论或书写的事物
senses.example: The subject of today's lesson is the weather.
senses.exampleCN: 今天这节课的主题是天气。
senses.why: This is the basic topic sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的主题义项。

senses.title: Course of study
senses.definition: an area of knowledge studied at school
senses.definitionCN: 在学校学习的一个知识领域
senses.example: History is her favourite subject.
senses.exampleCN: 历史是她最喜欢的科目。
senses.why: A topic of study becomes a school subject.
senses.whyCN: 被研究的主题成了学校科目。

senses.title: Person studied
senses.definition: a person or thing used in a test or study
senses.definitionCN: 用于测试或研究的人或物
senses.example: The subjects were asked to sleep well.
senses.exampleCN: 受试者被要求好好睡觉。
senses.why: Research places people under study.
senses.whyCN: 研究把人置于被观察的位置。

senses.title: Affected by
senses.definition: likely to be affected by something
senses.definitionCN: 容易受到某事影响的
senses.example: The schedule is subject to change.
senses.exampleCN: 日程可能会有变动。
senses.why: Being under control becomes being open to change.
senses.whyCN: 处于控制之下，引申为易受变动影响。

intro.en: Subject comes from Latin words meaning thrown under.
intro.cn: subject 来自拉丁语，意为被置于下方。

items.en: Subicere meant to throw under.
Subiectus meant placed under authority.
items.cn: subiectus 意为置于权力之下。

items.en: Sujet named a topic or a person ruled.
items.cn: sujet 指话题或被统治的人。

items.en: Subject named both a topic and a ruled person.
items.cn: subject 既指话题，也指臣民。

items.en: Subject became a school course and a study object.
items.cn: subject 成为学校科目和研究对象。

note.en: Subject is compared with look-alike words and with words for topics.
note.cn: 把 subject 与形近词以及表示主题的词作比较。

entries.definition: a thing you can see or touch
the main idea of a work

normalIntro.en: A subject is what a lesson, a study, or a ruler places under attention.
normalIntro.cn: subject 是课程、研究或统治者置于关注之下的东西。

normal.en: The subject of today's lesson is the weather.
normal.cn: 今天这节课的主题是天气。

normal.en: History is her favourite subject.
normal.cn: 历史是她最喜欢的科目。

normal.en: The subjects were asked to sleep well.
normal.cn: 受试者被要求好好睡觉。

normal.en: The schedule is subject to change.
Let us change the subject.

abstract.en: Every subject is a world someone chose to look at.
abstract.cn: 每个主题，都是有人选择去看的一个世界。

abstract.en: To be subject to time is to be human.
abstract.cn: 受时间支配，就是做人。

abstract.en: The subject of a life is rarely written down.
abstract.cn: 一生的主题，很少被写下来。

examples.en: The subject of today's lesson is the weather.
examples.cn: 今天这节课的主题是天气。

examples.en: History is her favourite subject.
examples.cn: 历史是她最喜欢的科目。

examples.en: The schedule is subject to change.

dict_mnemonic.text: subject 是「主题」，也指学校「科目」和研究「对象」；be subject to 是易受……影响，change the subject 是换个话题，subject matter 是题材。

root: 来自拉丁语 subicere（置于下方）的过去分词 subiectus，经古法语 sujet 进入英语；由被置于权力之下，引申为被讨论、被研究、被教授的对象，以及易受某种影响。

sensesIntro.en: Subject is a topic, a school course, a study object, or being open to an effect.
sensesIntro.cn: subject 是主题、学校科目、研究对象，或易受某影响。

core.en: Something placed under the eyes of others.
core.cn: 被放到众人目光之下的东西。

branches.en: The subject of today's lesson is the weather.
branches.cn: 今天这节课的主题是天气。

branches.en: History is her favourite subject.
branches.cn: 历史是她最喜欢的科目。

branches.en: The subjects were asked to sleep well.
branches.cn: 受试者被要求好好睡觉。

branches.en: The schedule is subject to change.
branches.cn: 日程可能会有变动。

branches.en: A course of study and a study object share one word.
branches.cn: 学习的科目和研究的对象共用一个词。

intro.en: Subject builds adjectives and nouns with -ive and -ion.
intro.cn: subject 借助 -ive 和 -ion 构成形容词和名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base iect- meant thrown.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 iect- 意为投掷。

items.meaning: a topic or a ruled person

items.example: He was subjecting them to questions.

items.exampleCN: 他们生活在被统治之中。

latinEntries.example: Subiectus gave English subject.
latinEntries.exampleCN: subiectus 演变为英语的 subject。

definition_en: to achieve what you wanted, or to take over from someone
core_image: 一步接一步走到底，终于站到了目标的位置
scene: 她努力了多年，终于成功了。After years of effort, she succeeded.
sceneCN: 这里 succeed 是「成功」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她努力了多年，终于成功了。

senses.title: Achieve
senses.definition: to achieve what you have been trying to do
senses.definitionCN: 达成一直想做之事
senses.example: After years of effort, she succeeded.
senses.exampleCN: 她努力了多年，终于成功了。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常使用的义项。

senses.title: Take over
senses.definition: to take the place of someone in an office
senses.definitionCN: 接替某人的职位
senses.example: She succeeded him as manager.
senses.exampleCN: 她接替他成为经理。
senses.why: One person follows another into a role.
senses.whyCN: 一个人跟着另一个人进入同一个位置。

senses.title: Follow in turn
senses.definition: to come next after something
senses.definitionCN: 紧跟在某事物之后出现
senses.example: Day succeeds day without pause.
senses.exampleCN: 日子一天接一天，从不停歇。
senses.why: The Latin root simply means to follow.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根本义就是跟随。

intro.en: Succeed comes from Latin for going up after another.
intro.cn: succeed 来自拉丁语，意为跟在别人之后走上来。

items.en: Cedere meant to go or yield.
Succedere meant to come after or take a place.
items.cn: succedere 意为随后而来或接替位置。

items.en: Succeder meant to follow or prosper.
items.cn: succeder 意为跟随或顺利发展。

items.en: Succeed meant to follow in office.
Succeed widened to mean achieve a goal.

note.en: Succeed is compared with look-alike words and with words for achieving.
note.cn: 把 succeed 与形近词以及表示取得成功的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: To succeed is to walk after something until you arrive.
normalIntro.cn: succeed 就是跟着目标一路走，直到抵达。

normal.en: After years of effort, she succeeded.
normal.cn: 她努力了多年，终于成功了。

normal.en: She succeeded him as manager.
Day succeeds day without pause.
normal.cn: 日子一天接一天，从不停歇。

normal.en: He succeeded in passing the exam.
The prince succeeded to the throne.

abstract.en: To succeed is to keep walking after the applause ends.
abstract.cn: 成功，是在掌声结束后继续走路。

abstract.en: Every success is a succession of small refusals.
abstract.cn: 每一次成功，都是一连串小小的不放弃。

abstract.en: What succeeds us will judge what we left.
abstract.cn: 接替我们的人，会评判我们留下的东西。

examples.en: After years of effort, she succeeded.
examples.cn: 她努力了多年，终于成功了。

examples.en: She succeeded him as manager.
He succeeded in passing the exam.

dict_mnemonic.text: succeed 是「成功」，也可表示「继任、接替」；succeed in 是在……方面成功，succeed to the throne 是继承王位，success 是成功，successor 是继任者。

root: 来自拉丁语 succedere，由 sub（在后、接近）与 cedere（走）组合，字面是「跟在后面走上来」；由接替位置，引申为顺利发展、达成目标。

sensesIntro.en: Succeed means to achieve a goal, to take over a role, or to come next.
sensesIntro.cn: succeed 表示达成目标、接替职位，或紧接着发生。

core.en: Stepping into the place someone else left.
core.cn: 走进别人离开后留下的位置。

branches.en: After years of effort, she succeeded.
branches.cn: 她努力了多年，终于成功了。

branches.en: She succeeded him as manager.
branches.cn: 她接替他成为经理。

branches.en: Day succeeds day without pause.
branches.cn: 日子一天接一天，从不停歇。

branches.en: Taking a role and reaching a goal both mean arriving.
branches.cn: 接替职位和达成目标，都意味着走到了。

branches.en: People and days both follow one another.
branches.cn: 人和日子，都是一个接一个。

intro.en: Succeed builds success, successful, and succession.
intro.cn: succeed 可构成 success、successful 和 succession。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base ced- meant to go.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 ced- 意为走。

items.example: Hard work succeeds in the end.

latinEntries.example: Cedere gave English succeed and proceed.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cedere 演变为英语的 succeed 和 proceed。

definition_en: of this kind, or to so great a degree
core_image: 手指向面前的东西，说「就是这一类」
scene: 我从未见过这样的景象。I have never seen such a sight.
sceneCN: 这里 such 是「这样的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：我从未见过这样的景象。

senses.title: Of this kind
senses.definition: of the kind already mentioned or understood
senses.definitionCN: 属于已经提到或暗指的那一类
senses.example: I have never seen such a sight.
senses.exampleCN: 我从未见过这样的景象。
senses.why: This is the basic sense of kind.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示种类的核心义项。

senses.title: So great
senses.definition: used to stress how great something is
senses.definitionCN: 用来强调某事物程度之高
senses.example: It was such a cold day.
senses.exampleCN: 那天真是冷极了。
senses.why: Here such marks degree, not kind.
senses.whyCN: 这里 such 标的是程度，而不是种类。

senses.title: For example
senses.definition: used to introduce one or more examples
senses.definitionCN: 用来引出一个或多个例子
senses.example: Fruits such as apples are cheap.
senses.exampleCN: 像苹果这样的水果很便宜。
senses.why: The phrase such as introduces examples.
senses.whyCN: 短语 such as 用来引出例子。

intro.en: Such is an old English compound of so and like.
intro.cn: such 是古英语中由 so 和 like 合成的词。

items.en: Swylc meant so formed or of this kind.
items.cn: swylc 意为如此形成的或这一类的。

items.en: Swylc came from swa and a word for body or form.
items.cn: swylc 由 swa 与表示形体或样子的词合成。

items.en: Such meant of this kind.
Such became common in comparisons of degree.
items.cn: such 常用于程度的比较。

items.en: Such as came to mean for example.
items.cn: such as 逐渐表示例如。

note.en: Such is compared with look-alike words and with words for similarity.
note.cn: 把 such 与形近词以及表示相似的词作比较。

entries.definition: to draw liquid into the mouth

normalIntro.en: Such points at a whole kind with one small word.
normalIntro.cn: such 用一个小词指向一整类事物。

normal.en: I have never seen such a sight.
normal.cn: 我从未见过这样的景象。

normal.en: It was such a cold day.
Fruits such as apples are cheap.
normal.cn: 像苹果这样的水果很便宜。

normal.en: There is no such rule.
He said such things before.

abstract.en: Such is a finger pointing at a whole family of things.
abstract.cn: such 是一根手指，指向一整类东西。

abstract.en: We fear such days because we remember them.
abstract.cn: 我们害怕这样的日子，因为记得它们。

abstract.en: No such thing lasts forever.
abstract.cn: 这样的东西，没有一样能永远持续。

examples.en: I have never seen such a sight.
examples.cn: 我从未见过这样的景象。

examples.en: Fruits such as apples are cheap.
examples.cn: 像苹果这样的水果很便宜。

examples.en: There is no such rule.

dict_mnemonic.text: such 是「这样的、如此的」；such as 表示例如，such a 表示这样一个，no such 表示没有这样的，as such 表示就其本身而言。

root: 来自古英语 swylc，由 swa（如此）与表示形体、样子的词合成，本义是「如此这般的」。

sensesIntro.en: Such marks a kind, stresses a degree, or introduces examples.
sensesIntro.cn: such 可以指某一类、强调程度，或引出例子。

core.en: Pointing at a kind of thing.

branches.en: I have never seen such a sight.
branches.cn: 我从未见过这样的景象。

branches.en: It was such a cold day.
branches.cn: 那天真是冷极了。

branches.en: Fruits such as apples are cheap.
branches.cn: 像苹果这样的水果很便宜。

branches.en: A kind and an example are close neighbors.
branches.cn: 种类和例子是近邻。

branches.en: Such heat is rare here.
branches.cn: 这样的高温在这里很少见。

intro.en: Such builds suchlike and such-and-such.
intro.cn: such 可构成 suchlike 和 such-and-such。

latinIntro.en: Such is an Old English word, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: such 是古英语词，而不是拉丁语。

items.example: Tools such as hammers are useful.
items.exampleCN: 像锤子这样的工具很有用。

items.meaning: in a way that results in
items.example: The door was such that it stuck.
Pens and suchlike are in the drawer.
items.exampleCN: 笔之类的东西在抽屉里。

items.example: He lives on such-and-such a street.
The idea, as such, is fine.
items.exampleCN: 这个想法本身没有问题。

definition_en: happening quickly and without warning
core_image: 平静的水面被一块石头砸开
scene: 一阵突然的冷风关上了门。A sudden cold wind closed the door.
sceneCN: 这里 sudden 是「突然的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一阵突然的冷风关上了门。

senses.title: Without warning
senses.definition: happening quickly and without warning
senses.definitionCN: 发生得很快且没有预兆
senses.example: A sudden cold wind closed the door.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵突然的冷风关上了门。
senses.why: This is the core sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义项。

senses.title: Unexpected
senses.definition: not expected and therefore surprising
senses.definitionCN: 没有预料到因而令人吃惊的
senses.example: His sudden departure surprised us.
senses.exampleCN: 他的突然离开让我们很意外。
senses.why: Here the stress is on surprise.
senses.whyCN: 这里强调令人意外。

intro.en: Sudden comes from Latin words for coming unexpectedly.
intro.cn: sudden 来自拉丁语，意为意外地到来。

items.en: Subitaneus meant coming suddenly.
Sodain meant sudden or hasty.
items.cn: sodain 意为突然的或仓促的。

items.en: Sudden meant happening without warning.
items.cn: sudden 意为没有预兆地发生。

items.en: Sudden kept the same sense.
items.cn: sudden 保持了相同的意思。

items.en: All of a sudden became a fixed phrase.
items.cn: all of a sudden 成为固定短语。

note.en: Sudden is compared with look-alike words and with words for quick events.
note.cn: 把 sudden 与形近词以及表示迅速发生的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Sudden is the moment before you have time to blink.
normalIntro.cn: sudden 就是你还没来得及眨眼的那一下。

normal.en: A sudden cold wind closed the door.
normal.cn: 一阵突然的冷风关上了门。

normal.en: His sudden departure surprised us.
normal.cn: 他的突然离开让我们很意外。

normal.en: There was a sudden change in the plan.
The car came to a sudden stop.
All of a sudden the room went dark.

abstract.en: Sudden things are remembered longer than slow ones.
abstract.cn: 突然发生的事，比缓慢发生的事记得更久。

abstract.en: We call it sudden because we were not looking.
abstract.cn: 我们称之为突然，只是因为我们没在看。

abstract.en: A sudden silence can be louder than a shout.
abstract.cn: 突然的安静，可能比喊叫更响。

examples.en: A sudden cold wind closed the door.
examples.cn: 一阵突然的冷风关上了门。

items.cn: 它又成为动词，表示晒太阳。

note.en: Sun is compared with look-alike words and with words for sunlight.
note.cn: 把 sun 与形近词以及表示阳光的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Sun is the star we see by day and the light it sends us.
normalIntro.cn: sun 是我们白天看见的那颗恒星，也是它送来的光。

normal.en: The sun came out from behind the clouds.
The sun rises early in summer.
Sit in the sun and warm up.
They sunned themselves on the beach.
The morning sun filled the room.

abstract.en: The sun asks for nothing and gives everything.
abstract.cn: 太阳一无所求，却给出一切。

abstract.en: Every shadow is proof that the sun is there.
abstract.cn: 每一道影子都证明太阳就在那里。

abstract.en: We turn toward light without being taught.
abstract.cn: 我们不用被教，就会转向光。

examples.en: The sun came out from behind the clouds.
The sun rises early in summer.
Sit in the sun and warm up.

dict_mnemonic.text: sun 是「太阳」，也指「阳光」，还可作动词表示晒太阳；sunny 是晴朗的，sunshine 是阳光，sunrise 与 sunset 分别是日出和日落。

root: 来自古英语 sunne，与德语 Sonne 同源，是日耳曼语中表示太阳的古老词。

sensesIntro.en: Sun means the star that lights the earth, its light, or to sit in its light.
sensesIntro.cn: sun 指照亮地球的恒星、它的光，也可作动词表示晒太阳。

core.en: The source of daylight and warmth.

branches.en: The sun came out from behind the clouds.
branches.cn: 太阳从云后出来了。

branches.en: The sun rises early in summer.
branches.cn: 夏天太阳升起得早。

branches.en: Sit in the sun and warm up.
branches.cn: 坐到阳光下暖和一下。

branches.en: They sunned themselves on the beach.
branches.cn: 他们在海滩上晒太阳。

branches.en: The star and its light share one word.
branches.cn: 恒星和它的光共用一个词。

intro.en: Sun builds sunny, sunshine, and many compounds such as sunrise.
intro.cn: sun 可构成 sunny、sunshine，以及 sunrise 等大量复合词。

latinIntro.en: Sun is Germanic rather than Latin in origin.
latinIntro.cn: sun 源自日耳曼语，而非拉丁语。

items.example: The room is full of sunshine.

latinEntries.example: Sunno is the old Germanic root of sun.
latinEntries.exampleCN: sunno 是 sun 的古老日耳曼词根。

definition_en: very good, or above the usual level
core_image: 一颗亮得耀眼的星星，比周围都大一圈
scene: 这家小餐馆的汤特别好喝。The soup at this small restaurant is super.
sceneCN: 这里 super 是「极好的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这家小餐馆的汤特别好喝。

senses.title: Very good
senses.definition: excellent, especially in speech
senses.definitionCN: 非常好，多用于口语
senses.example: The soup at this small restaurant is super.
senses.exampleCN: 这家小餐馆的汤特别好喝。
senses.why: This is the colloquial praise sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是口语中的称赞义项。

senses.title: Above the usual level
senses.definition: larger or higher than normal
senses.definitionCN: 比一般更大或更高
senses.example: The city built a super highway.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市修建了一条超级公路。
senses.why: Here super works like a prefix meaning beyond.
senses.whyCN: 这里 super 像前缀一样表示超出。

intro.en: Super comes from Latin super, above.
intro.cn: super 来自拉丁语 super，意为在上、超过。

items.en: Super meant above or over.
Super worked mostly as a prefix.
items.cn: super 主要作为前缀使用。

items.en: Super meant above or beyond.
It became a word for very good.
items.cn: 它成为一个表示极好的词。

items.en: It formed supermarket and superman.
items.cn: 它构成了 supermarket 和 superman。

note.en: Super is compared with look-alike words and with words for excellence.
note.cn: 把 super 与形近词以及表示优秀的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Super means above, so a super thing stands above the ordinary.
normalIntro.cn: super 意为在上，所以 super 的东西高出平常。

normal.en: The soup at this small restaurant is super.
normal.cn: 这家小餐馆的汤特别好喝。

normal.en: We had a super time at the beach.
normal.cn: 我们在海滩玩得非常开心。

normal.en: The train was super quick.
That is a super idea.
The children were super excited.

abstract.en: Super is praise with the roof taken off.
abstract.cn: super 是掀掉屋顶的赞美。

abstract.en: What stands above us can also lift us.
abstract.cn: 高于我们的东西，也能把我们托起。

abstract.en: A super day is often a simple day.
abstract.cn: 超级好的一天，往往是简单的一天。

examples.en: The soup at this small restaurant is super.
examples.cn: 这家小餐馆的汤特别好喝。

examples.en: We had a super time at the beach.
examples.cn: 我们在海滩玩得非常开心。

examples.en: That is a super idea.

dict_mnemonic.text: super 来自拉丁语「在上」，口语中表示「极好的」，作前缀表示「超级、超出」，如 supermarket、superman、supernatural。

root: 来自拉丁语 super（在上、超过），由空间上的「在上」引申为等级与质量上的「超出一般」。

sensesIntro.en: Super means very good in speech, or above the usual level as a prefix-like word.
sensesIntro.cn: super 在口语中表示极好的，也可像前缀一样表示超出一般。

core.en: Above the ordinary line.

branches.en: The soup at this small restaurant is super.
branches.cn: 这家小餐馆的汤特别好喝。

branches.en: We had a super time at the beach.
branches.cn: 我们在海滩玩得非常开心。

branches.en: The city built a super highway.
branches.cn: 这座城市修建了一条超级公路。

branches.en: Above normal and very good meet in one word.
branches.cn: 超出平常与非常好在一个词里相遇。

branches.en: That is a super idea.
branches.cn: 那是个极好的主意。

intro.en: Super works as a prefix in superb, superior, and supermarket.
intro.cn: super 在 superb、superior 和 supermarket 中作前缀。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin super, above.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根是拉丁语 super，意为在上。

items.exampleCN: 这个故事有超自然元素。

latinEntries.example: Super is the source of super and its compounds.
latinEntries.exampleCN: super 是 super 及其复合词的来源。

definition_en: a large self-service shop selling food and household goods
core_image: 一排排货架之间，顾客推着购物车慢慢走
scene: 她在超市买了水果和牛奶。She bought fruit and milk at the supermarket.
sceneCN: 这里 supermarket 是「超级市场」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她在超市买了水果和牛奶。

senses.title: A large self-service shop
senses.definition: a large shop where customers serve themselves
senses.definitionCN: 顾客自行取货的大型商店
senses.example: She bought fruit and milk at the supermarket.
senses.exampleCN: 她在超市买了水果和牛奶。
senses.why: This is the everyday place sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常的地点义项。

senses.title: A chain of such shops
senses.definition: a company that runs many such shops
senses.definitionCN: 经营多家此类商店的公司
senses.example: The supermarket opened ten new branches.
senses.exampleCN: 这家连锁超市新开了十家分店。
senses.why: Here the word names the business, not one shop.
senses.whyCN: 这里指企业，而不是单家门店。

intro.en: Supermarket joins super, beyond, with market, a place of trade.
intro.cn: supermarket 由 super（超出）与 market（市场）组合而成。

items.en: Mercatus meant trade or market.
Market meant a place of trade.
Market meant a public place of selling.
items.cn: market 指公开售货的场所。

items.en: Supermarket meant a very large market.
items.cn: supermarket 指规模很大的市场。

items.en: It spread worldwide as a shop type.
items.cn: 它作为店铺类型传遍世界。

note.en: Supermarket is compared with look-alike words and with other places to shop.
note.cn: 把 supermarket 与形近词以及其他购物场所作比较。

entries.definition: a place where goods are sold

normalIntro.en: A supermarket is a market grown large enough to hold everything.
normalIntro.cn: 超市就是一个大到能装下一切的市场。

normal.en: She bought fruit and milk at the supermarket.
normal.cn: 她在超市买了水果和牛奶。

normal.en: The supermarket opens at eight.
We pushed a trolley around the supermarket.
normal.cn: 我们推着购物车在超市里走。

normal.en: The supermarket chain opened ten new branches.
normal.cn: 这家连锁超市新开了十家分店。

normal.en: The local supermarket hires many students.
normal.cn: 当地超市雇了许多学生。

abstract.en: A supermarket is abundance arranged in rows.
abstract.cn: 超市，是排成行的丰盛。

abstract.en: Everything is within reach, and that is the point.
abstract.cn: 一切都触手可及，这正是它的意义。

abstract.en: We shop quickly and forget how far the food travelled.
abstract.cn: 我们买得很快，却忘了食物走了多远。

examples.en: She bought fruit and milk at the supermarket.
examples.cn: 她在超市买了水果和牛奶。

examples.en: The supermarket opens at eight.
We pushed a trolley around the supermarket.
examples.cn: 我们推着购物车在超市里走。

dict_mnemonic.text: supermarket 由 super（超级）与 market（市场）构成，表示超市；supermarket chain 是连锁超市。

root: 由 super（超级、超出）与 market（市场）复合而成，指规模超出传统市场的大型自选商店。

sensesIntro.en: Supermarket means a large self-service shop, or the company that runs such shops.
sensesIntro.cn: supermarket 表示大型自选商店，也可指经营这类门店的公司。

core.en: A market made large and self-service.

branches.en: She bought fruit and milk at the supermarket.
branches.cn: 她在超市买了水果和牛奶。

branches.en: We pushed a trolley around the supermarket.
branches.cn: 我们推着购物车在超市里走。

branches.en: The supermarket chain opened ten new branches.
branches.cn: 这家连锁超市新开了十家分店。

branches.en: One shop and a whole chain share the name.
branches.cn: 一家店和整个连锁共用一个名字。

branches.en: The supermarket opens at eight.
branches.cn: 超市八点开门。

intro.en: Supermarket combines super and market; market builds marketplace.
intro.cn: supermarket 由 super 与 market 组合，market 还能构成 marketplace。

latinIntro.en: Market comes from Latin mercatus, trade.
latinIntro.cn: market 来自拉丁语 mercatus，意为交易。

latinEntries.example: Mercatus is the source of market.
latinEntries.exampleCN: mercatus 是 market 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Super is the first part of supermarket.
latinEntries.exampleCN: super 是 supermarket 的第一个部分。

definition_en: to provide something needed, or the amount provided
core_image: 一辆货车把新鲜蔬菜卸到商店门口
scene: 这家农场向本地商店供应蔬菜。The farm supplies vegetables to local shops.
sceneCN: 这里 supply 是「供应」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这家农场向本地商店供应蔬菜。

senses.title: To provide
senses.definition: to give or sell something that is needed
senses.definitionCN: 给出或出售所需要的东西
senses.example: The farm supplies vegetables to local shops.
senses.exampleCN: 这家农场向本地商店供应蔬菜。
senses.why: This is the main verb sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是主要的动词义项。

senses.title: The amount available
senses.definition: the amount of something available
senses.definitionCN: 可获得的东西的数量
senses.example: The water supply is limited.
senses.exampleCN: 供水是有限的。
senses.why: Here the word is a noun of amount.
senses.whyCN: 这里指数量的名词。

senses.title: Goods for a need
senses.definition: food and equipment needed for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某一目的需要的食物与装备
senses.example: They carried medical supplies.
senses.exampleCN: 他们携带医疗物资。
senses.why: This plural sense names concrete goods.
senses.whyCN: 这个复数义项指具体物资。

intro.en: Supply comes from Latin supplere, to fill up.
intro.cn: supply 来自拉丁语 supplere，意为填满、补足。

items.en: Sub meant under.
Plere meant to fill.
Suppleer meant to fill a need.
Supply meant to provide.
It also meant the amount provided.

note.en: Supply is compared with look-alike words and with verbs of providing.
note.cn: 把 supply 与形近词以及表示提供的动词作比较。

entries.definition: to ask formally or to put on

normalIntro.en: To supply is to fill the empty space in someone's need.
normalIntro.cn: supply 就是填满别人需求里的空位。

normal.en: The farm supplies vegetables to local shops.
normal.cn: 这家农场向本地商店供应蔬菜。

normal.en: The water supply is limited.
They carried medical supplies.
Demand is rising faster than supply.
Fresh water is in short supply here.

abstract.en: Supply is a promise made in goods.
abstract.cn: 供应，是用货物许下的承诺。

abstract.en: What is in short supply becomes precious.
abstract.cn: 供应不足的东西会变得珍贵。

abstract.en: A chain of supply is a chain of trust.
abstract.cn: 供应链，也是一条信任链。

examples.en: The farm supplies vegetables to local shops.
examples.cn: 这家农场向本地商店供应蔬菜。

examples.en: The water supply is limited.
They carried medical supplies.

dict_mnemonic.text: supply 是「供应」，也可作名词表示供应量；supplies 指补给品，supply and demand 是供求，supplier 是供应商。

root: 来自拉丁语 supplere（填满），由 sub（在下）与 plere（填满）组成，后经古法语进入英语，表示提供所需。

sensesIntro.en: Supply means to provide something needed, the amount available, or the goods provided.
sensesIntro.cn: supply 表示提供所需之物、可获得的供应量，或所提供的物资。

core.en: Filling a need with goods.

branches.en: The farm supplies vegetables to local shops.
branches.cn: 这家农场向本地商店供应蔬菜。

branches.en: The water supply is limited.
branches.cn: 供水是有限的。

branches.en: They carried medical supplies.
branches.cn: 他们携带医疗物资。

branches.en: The act and the amount share one word.
branches.cn: 供应动作与供应量共用一个词。

branches.en: Fresh water is in short supply here.
branches.cn: 这里淡水供应不足。

intro.en: Supply builds supplier and supplies, and shares a root with supplement.
intro.cn: supply 可构成 supplier 和 supplies，并与 supplement 同根。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin plere, to fill.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根是拉丁语 plere，意为填满。

latinEntries.example: Supplere is the source of supply.
latinEntries.exampleCN: supplere 是 supply 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Plere also gave English complete.
latinEntries.exampleCN: plere 也演变为英语的 complete。

definition_en: to help or hold something up, or to provide for someone
core_image: 两根柱子稳稳托住屋顶
scene: 家人支持她的决定。Her family supported her decision.
sceneCN: 这里 support 是「支持」（第 1 个义项）；句意：家人支持她的决定。

senses.title: To back someone
senses.definition: to help someone or agree with a plan
senses.definitionCN: 帮助某人或赞成某个计划
senses.example: Her family supported her decision.
senses.exampleCN: 家人支持她的决定。
senses.why: This is the main social sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是主要的社会关系义项。

senses.title: To hold up
senses.definition: to carry the weight of something
senses.definitionCN: 承受某物的重量
senses.example: The columns support the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 这些柱子支撑着屋顶。
senses.why: This is the physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是物理义项。

senses.title: Help or a prop
senses.definition: help given, or a thing that holds something up
senses.definitionCN: 给予的帮助，或托住某物的东西
senses.example: The bridge needs more support.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥需要更多支撑。
senses.why: This noun covers help and structure.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词涵盖帮助与支撑结构。

senses.title: To provide for
senses.definition: to pay for the needs of someone
senses.definitionCN: 负担某人的生活需要
senses.example: He supports a family of four.
senses.exampleCN: 他供养四口之家。
senses.why: Here support means money and care.
senses.whyCN: 这里指金钱与生活照料。

intro.en: Support comes from Latin supportare, to carry from below.
intro.cn: support 来自拉丁语 supportare，意为从下面承载。

items.en: Sub meant under.
Portare meant to carry.
Supportare meant to carry from below.
Supporter meant to bear or help.
Support meant to hold up and to help.

note.en: Support is compared with look-alike words and with verbs of helping.
note.cn: 把 support 与形近词以及表示帮助的动词作比较。

normalIntro.en: To support is to put your strength under someone else's weight.
normalIntro.cn: support 就是把自己的力量垫在别人的重量下面。

normal.en: Her family supported her decision.
The columns support the roof.
The bridge needs more support.
He supports a family of four.
Thank you for your strong support.

abstract.en: Support is strength lent to another.
abstract.cn: 支持，是借给别人的力量。

abstract.en: A roof forgets the columns that hold it.
abstract.cn: 屋顶会忘记托住它的柱子。

abstract.en: What we support, we help to stand.
abstract.cn: 我们支持什么，就是帮助什么站立。

examples.en: Her family supported her decision.
The columns support the roof.
He supports a family of four.

dict_mnemonic.text: support 是「支持、支撑」，也可指「供养」；supporter 是支持者，supportive 是支持的，financial support 是经济支持。

root: 来自拉丁语 supportare（从下面承载），由 sub（在下）与 portare（携带）组成，后引申为支持与供养。

sensesIntro.en: Support means to back someone, hold something up, provide for someone, or the help itself.
sensesIntro.cn: support 表示支持某人、支撑某物、供养某人，或指帮助本身。

core.en: Strength placed under a weight.

branches.en: Her family supported her decision.
branches.cn: 家人支持她的决定。

branches.en: The columns support the roof.
branches.cn: 这些柱子支撑着屋顶。

branches.en: The bridge needs more support.
branches.cn: 这座桥需要更多支撑。

branches.en: He supports a family of four.
branches.cn: 他供养四口之家。

branches.en: People and pillars both keep things standing.
branches.cn: 人和柱子都能让东西立住。

intro.en: Support builds supporter and supportive.
intro.cn: support 可构成 supporter 和 supportive。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin portare, to carry, with sub under.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是拉丁语 portare（携带），加上 sub（在下）。

latinEntries.example: Portare is the root of support.
latinEntries.exampleCN: portare 是 support 的词根。

latinEntries.example: Supportare led to French supporter.
latinEntries.exampleCN: supportare 演变为法语 supporter。

definition_en: to think that something is probably true, or to imagine it for an argument
core_image: 一个人闭上眼，据桌上的线索猜测答案
scene: 我猜他已经在路上了。I suppose he is already on his way.
sceneCN: 这里 suppose 是「猜想」（第 1 个义项）；句意：我猜他已经在路上了。

senses.title: To think probably
senses.definition: to think something is probably true
senses.definitionCN: 认为某事很可能是真的
senses.example: I suppose he is already on his way.
senses.exampleCN: 我猜他已经在路上了。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常义项。

senses.title: To imagine for argument
senses.definition: to imagine something as a starting point
senses.definitionCN: 把某事当作推理的起点
senses.example: Suppose you had one more day.
senses.exampleCN: 假设你再多一天时间。
senses.why: Here the word sets up a condition.
senses.whyCN: 这里是在设定条件。

senses.title: To be expected to
senses.definition: to be expected or required to do something
senses.definitionCN: 被期望或被要求做某事
senses.example: You are supposed to sign here.
senses.exampleCN: 你应该在这里签名。
senses.why: This is the fixed be supposed to pattern.
senses.whyCN: 这是 be supposed to 的固定用法。

intro.en: Suppose comes from Latin supponere, to put under.
intro.cn: suppose 来自拉丁语 supponere，意为放在下面。

items.en: Sub meant under.
Ponere meant to put.
Supponere meant to put underneath.
Supposer meant to assume.
Suppose meant to think or assume.

note.en: Suppose is compared with look-alike words and with verbs of assuming.
note.cn: 把 suppose 与形近词以及表示假定的动词作比较。

entries.definition: to take as true without proof
to form a picture in the mind

normalIntro.en: To suppose is to place an idea under a question and see if it holds.
normalIntro.cn: suppose 就是把一个想法放到问题下面，看它是否站得住。

normal.en: I suppose he is already on his way.
Suppose you had one more day.
You are supposed to sign here.
I suppose so, but I am not sure.
normal.cn: 我想是这样，但我不确定。

normal.en: Do you suppose she will come?

abstract.en: To suppose is to lend the mind a temporary truth.
abstract.cn: 猜想，是把一个临时的真相借给头脑。

abstract.en: Every science begins with suppose.
abstract.cn: 每一门科学都始于假设。

abstract.en: We suppose more often than we notice.
abstract.cn: 我们猜想的次数，比我们注意到的更多。

examples.en: I suppose he is already on his way.
Suppose you had one more day.
You are supposed to sign here.

dict_mnemonic.text: suppose 是「猜想、假设」，be supposed to 表示「应该」；I suppose so 是我想是这样。

root: 来自拉丁语 supponere（放在下面），由 sub（在下）与 ponere（放置）组成，意为把想法放在下面作为基础，即假设、猜想。

sensesIntro.en: Suppose means to think something is likely, to imagine a case, or in be supposed to, to be expected to.
sensesIntro.cn: suppose 表示认为某事很可能、设想一种情况，或在 be supposed to 中表示应该。

core.en: An idea placed under a question.
core.cn: 放在问题下面的一个想法。

branches.en: I suppose he is already on his way.
branches.cn: 我猜他已经在路上了。

branches.en: I suppose so, but I am not sure.
branches.cn: 我想是这样，但我不确定。

branches.en: Suppose you had one more day.
branches.cn: 假设你再多一天时间。

branches.en: You are supposed to sign here.
branches.cn: 你应该在这里签名。

branches.en: A guess today can become a premise tomorrow.
branches.cn: 今天的猜想，明天可能成为前提。

intro.en: Suppose builds supposed, supposedly, and supposition.
intro.cn: suppose 可构成 supposed、supposedly 和 supposition。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin ponere, to put.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根是拉丁语 ponere，意为放置。

items.example: The theory rests on a supposition.
items.exampleCN: 这个理论建立在一个假设上。

latinEntries.example: Supponere is the source of suppose.
latinEntries.exampleCN: supponere 是 suppose 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Ponere also gave English position.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ponere 也演变为英语的 position。

definition_en: certain that something is true or will happen
core_image: 一个人点头，把手放在心口表示确定
scene: 我确信自己锁了门。I am sure that I locked the door.
sceneCN: 这里 sure 是「确信的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：我确信自己锁了门。

senses.title: Certain in your mind
senses.definition: feeling no doubt about something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事没有怀疑
senses.example: I am sure that I locked the door.
senses.exampleCN: 我确信自己锁了门。
senses.why: This sense describes a person's confidence.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项描述人的把握。

senses.title: Certain to happen
senses.definition: certain to happen or be true
senses.definitionCN: 注定会发生或确实如此
senses.example: It is sure to rain tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚一定会下雨。
senses.why: Here the word describes the event.
senses.whyCN: 这里描述的是事情本身。

senses.title: Certainly, in speech
senses.definition: used in speech to mean certainly
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示当然
senses.example: Sure, I can help you.
senses.exampleCN: 当然，我可以帮你。
senses.why: This is the short spoken reply.
senses.whyCN: 这是简短的口语回应。

intro.en: Sure comes from Latin securus, free from care.
intro.cn: sure 来自拉丁语 securus，意为无忧的、安心的。

items.en: Securus meant free from care.
Seur meant safe or certain.
items.cn: seur 意为安全的、确定的。

items.en: Sure meant safe and certain.
items.cn: sure 意为安全而确定的。

items.en: Sure meant having no doubt.
It became a spoken word for certainly.

note.en: Sure is compared with look-alike words and with words for certainty.
note.cn: 把 sure 与形近词以及表示确定的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Sure is a mind with no question left open.
normalIntro.cn: sure 是心里没有留下问题的状态。

normal.en: I am sure that I locked the door.
Make sure the window is closed.
It is sure to rain tonight.
Sure, I can help you.
Are you quite sure about the time?

abstract.en: Sure is a door closed quietly on doubt.
abstract.cn: 确定，是轻轻把怀疑关在门外。

abstract.en: Few things are as sure as we feel.
abstract.cn: 很少有事情像我们感觉的那样确定。

abstract.en: To be sure is to rest, if only for a moment.
abstract.cn: 确定，就是休息一下，哪怕只有片刻。

examples.en: I am sure that I locked the door.
Make sure the window is closed.
Sure, I can help you.

dict_mnemonic.text: sure 是「确信的、一定的」，make sure 是确保，for sure 是确实；口语中 sure 也可表示「当然」。

root: 来自拉丁语 securus（无忧的），经古法语 seur 进入英语，由「安心」引申为「确定」。

sensesIntro.en: Sure means feeling certain, certain to happen, or certainly in speech.
sensesIntro.cn: sure 表示心里确信、某事必然发生，或口语中的「当然」。

core.en: A mind at rest about the truth.

branches.en: I am sure that I locked the door.
branches.cn: 我确信自己锁了门。

branches.en: Are you quite sure about the time?
branches.cn: 你十分确定时间吗？

branches.en: It is sure to rain tonight.
branches.cn: 今晚一定会下雨。

branches.en: Sure, I can help you.
branches.cn: 当然，我可以帮你。

branches.en: People and events can both be sure.
branches.cn: 人和事都可以是确定的。

intro.en: Sure builds surely, surety, and assure.
intro.cn: sure 可构成 surely、surety 和 assure。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin securus, free from care.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根是拉丁语 securus，意为无忧的。

items.example: He was unsure of the way.
I assure you it is safe.
items.exampleCN: 我向你保证它是安全的。

latinEntries.example: Securus is the source of sure.
latinEntries.exampleCN: securus 是 sure 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Cura forms the second part of securus.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cura 是 securus 的第二个部分。

definition_en: an unexpected event or feeling, or to cause that feeling
core_image: 打开盒子的一瞬间，人们露出吃惊的表情
scene: 他的回答让大家十分惊讶。His answer caused great surprise.
sceneCN: 这里 surprise 是「惊讶」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他的回答让大家十分惊讶。

senses.title: The feeling of shock
senses.definition: the feeling caused by something unexpected
senses.definitionCN: 由意外之事引起的感受
senses.example: His answer caused great surprise.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回答让大家十分惊讶。
senses.why: This is the core feeling sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的情绪义项。

senses.title: An unexpected event
senses.definition: something that happens without being expected
senses.definitionCN: 没有预料到而发生的事
senses.example: The party was a complete surprise.
senses.exampleCN: 这场聚会完全是个惊喜。
senses.why: Here the word names the event, not the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 这里指事件而非感受。

senses.title: To cause surprise
senses.definition: to make someone feel sudden wonder
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到突然的惊奇
senses.example: The news surprised everyone in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 这个消息让房间里所有人都感到惊讶。
senses.why: As a verb it names the act of causing the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 作动词时指引发这种感受。

intro.en: Surprise came from a French verb meaning to overtake suddenly.
intro.cn: surprise 来自一个意为「突然赶上」的法语动词。

items.en: Super meant over or above.
Prehendere meant to seize.
Surprendre meant to overtake.
Surprise meant a sudden attack.
Surprise came to mean sudden wonder.
items.cn: surprise 转而表示突然的惊奇。

note.en: Surprise is compared with look-alike sur- words and with words for wonder.
note.cn: 把 surprise 与形近的 sur- 词以及表示惊奇的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Surprise moves from sudden seizure to sudden wonder.
normalIntro.cn: surprise 从突然抓住演变为突然惊奇。

normal.en: His answer caused great surprise.
normal.cn: 他的回答让大家十分惊讶。

normal.en: The party was a complete surprise.
normal.cn: 这场聚会完全是个惊喜。

normal.en: The news surprised everyone in the room.
normal.cn: 这个消息让房间里所有人都感到惊讶。

normal.en: She looked up in surprise.
To my surprise, the shop was still open.
normal.cn: 令我惊讶的是，商店还开着。

abstract.en: Surprise is what happens when the world outruns our plan.
abstract.cn: 当世界跑得比计划快时，惊讶就发生了。

abstract.en: The word once meant a sudden attack, which is also a kind of surprise.
abstract.cn: 这个词曾指突然袭击，那也是惊讶的一种。

abstract.en: A surprise interrupts time for a moment.
abstract.cn: 意外之事会让时间停顿片刻。

examples.en: His answer caused great surprise.
examples.cn: 他的回答让大家十分惊讶。

examples.en: The party was a complete surprise.
examples.cn: 这场聚会完全是个惊喜。

examples.en: To my surprise, the shop was still open.
examples.cn: 令我惊讶的是，商店还开着。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 突然抓住
dict_mnemonic.text: surprise 原指「突然抓住、突袭」，后来指被意外之事「抓住」的感觉，即惊讶。

root: 源自拉丁语 super（在上）与 prehendere（抓住），经古法语 surprendre（突然赶上）进入英语，由突袭引申为惊讶。

sensesIntro.en: Surprise means the feeling of wonder, an unexpected event, or to cause that feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: surprise 指惊奇之感、意外之事，或使某人惊奇。

core.en: Being caught by what we did not expect.

branches.en: His answer caused great surprise.
branches.cn: 他的回答让大家十分惊讶。

branches.en: She looked up in surprise.
branches.cn: 她惊讶地抬起头。

branches.en: The party was a complete surprise.
branches.cn: 这场聚会完全是个惊喜。

branches.en: The news surprised everyone in the room.
branches.cn: 这个消息让房间里所有人都感到惊讶。

branches.en: A surprising event and the feeling it brings share one word.
branches.cn: 意外事件与其带来的感受共用一个词。

intro.en: Surprise forms surprised, surprising, and surprisingly.
intro.cn: surprise 可构成 surprised、surprising 与 surprisingly。

latinIntro.en: The Latin prehendere also hides in comprehend and apprehend.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 prehendere 也藏在 comprehend 与 apprehend 中。

items.example: We were surprised by the news.
items.exampleCN: 我们被这个消息惊到了。
他们策划了一场惊喜聚会。

items.example: The visit was a pleasant surprise.

latinEntries.example: Prehendere is behind surprise.
latinEntries.exampleCN: prehendere 是 surprise 的深层来源。

latinEntries.example: Super adds the sense of over.
latinEntries.exampleCN: super 增加「在上」之义。

definition_en: a study of opinions or facts, or to look over an area
core_image: 研究员拿着问卷站在街角，记录路人的回答
scene: 研究者调查了五百名居民。The researchers surveyed five hundred residents.
sceneCN: 这里 survey 是「调查」（第 1 个义项）；句意：研究者调查了五百名居民。

senses.title: A study of opinions
senses.definition: a set of questions used to collect opinions or facts
senses.definitionCN: 用于收集意见或事实的一组问题
senses.example: The researchers surveyed five hundred residents.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者调查了五百名居民。
senses.why: This is the common social-science sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是常见的社会科学义项。

senses.title: The measuring of land
senses.definition: the act of measuring land or an area
senses.definitionCN: 测量土地或区域的行为
senses.example: They surveyed the land before building.
senses.exampleCN: 建房前他们勘测了土地。
senses.why: This is the older technical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是较旧的技术义项。

senses.title: A general view
senses.definition: a broad look at a whole subject
senses.definitionCN: 对整体主题的总体观察
senses.example: The book gives a survey of modern art.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书对现代艺术作了概览。
senses.why: Here the word means looking over the whole.
senses.whyCN: 这里指通览整体。

intro.en: Survey came from a French verb meaning to oversee.
intro.cn: survey 来自一个意为「俯视、查看」的法语动词。

items.en: Super meant over.
Videre meant to see.
Surveoir meant to oversee.
Survey meant a formal inspection.
Survey extended to opinion studies.

note.en: Survey is compared with look-alike sur- words and with words for study.
note.cn: 把 survey 与形近的 sur- 词以及表示研究的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Survey means looking over a group or a piece of land.
normalIntro.cn: survey 指查看一群人或者一片土地。

normal.en: The researchers surveyed five hundred residents.
normal.cn: 研究者调查了五百名居民。

normal.en: They surveyed the land before building.
normal.cn: 建房前他们勘测了土地。

normal.en: The book gives a survey of modern art.
normal.cn: 这本书对现代艺术作了概览。

normal.en: The survey results surprised the company.
normal.cn: 调查结果让公司很惊讶。

normal.en: A team surveyed the coast last month.
normal.cn: 一个团队上个月勘测了海岸。

abstract.en: A survey is a way of seeing a whole without touching every part.
abstract.cn: 调查是一种不必触碰每一处而看见整体的方式。

abstract.en: The word once meant to look down from above.
abstract.cn: 这个词原指从上方俯视。

abstract.en: To survey is to turn scattered facts into a shape.
abstract.cn: 调查就是散乱的事实变成形状。

examples.en: The researchers surveyed five hundred residents.
examples.cn: 研究者调查了五百名居民。

examples.en: They surveyed the land before building.
examples.cn: 建房前他们勘测了土地。

examples.en: The survey results surprised the company.
examples.cn: 调查结果让公司很惊讶。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 俯视查看
dict_mnemonic.text: survey 来自法语 surveoir（俯视、查看），所以既能表示「调查」，也能表示「测量、概览」。

root: 源自拉丁语 super（在上）与 videre（看），经古法语 surveoir 进入英语，核心是从整体上查看。

sensesIntro.en: Survey means a study of opinions, the measuring of land, or a broad view.
sensesIntro.cn: survey 指意见调查、土地测量，或整体概览。

core.en: Looking over a whole from above.

branches.en: The researchers surveyed five hundred residents.
branches.cn: 研究者调查了五百名居民。

branches.en: The survey results surprised the company.
branches.cn: 调查结果让公司很惊讶。

branches.en: They surveyed the land before building.
branches.cn: 建房前他们勘测了土地。

branches.en: The book gives a survey of modern art.
branches.cn: 这本书对现代艺术作了概览。

branches.en: Opinions and land can both be surveyed.
branches.cn: 意见与土地都可以被调查或测量。

intro.en: Survey forms surveyor and surveying.
intro.cn: survey 可构成 surveyor 与 surveying。

latinIntro.en: The Latin videre, to see, also appears in video and vision.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre（看见）也出现在 video 与 vision 中。

latinEntries.example: Videre is the seeing root of survey.
latinEntries.exampleCN: videre 是 survey 的「看」词根。

latinEntries.example: Super gives survey its over sense.
latinEntries.exampleCN: super 赋予 survey「在上」之义。

definition_en: tasting like sugar, pleasant and gentle, or a small piece of candy
core_image: 一块蜂蜜蛋糕上闪着糖霜的光
scene: 这块蛋糕太甜了，她只吃了一半。The cake was too sweet, so she ate only half.
sceneCN: 这里 sweet 是「甜的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这块蛋糕太甜了，她只吃了一半。

senses.title: Tasting like sugar
senses.definition: having the taste of sugar or honey
senses.definitionCN: 有糖或蜂蜜的味道
senses.example: The cake was too sweet, so she ate only half.
senses.exampleCN: 这块蛋糕太甜了，她只吃了一半。
senses.why: This is the basic sense of taste.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的味觉义项。

senses.title: Pleasant and gentle
senses.definition: pleasant, kind, or gentle to the senses
senses.definitionCN: 令人愉快、和善或柔和的
senses.example: She has a sweet voice.
senses.exampleCN: 她的嗓音很悦耳。
senses.why: Pleasant taste becomes pleasant manner.
senses.whyCN: 愉快的味道变成愉快的态度。

senses.title: A piece of candy
senses.definition: a small sweet food made of sugar
senses.definitionCN: 糖制成的小甜食
senses.example: She gave the child a sweet.
senses.exampleCN: 她给了孩子一颗糖。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for candy.
senses.whyCN: 形容词变成表示糖果的名词。

intro.en: Sweet is an old Germanic word for the taste of sugar and honey.
intro.cn: sweet 是表示糖与蜂蜜味道的古老日耳曼词。

items.en: Swotja meant sweet.
Swete meant sweet.
Swete meant pleasing to taste.
Sweet extended to sounds and manners.
items.cn: sweet 扩展到声音与举止。

items.en: Sweet became a noun for candy.
items.cn: sweet 成为表示糖果的名词。

note.en: Sweet is compared with look-alike words and with words for sugary taste.
note.cn: 把 sweet 与形近词以及表示甜味的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Sweet joins the tongue, the ear and the heart.
normalIntro.cn: sweet 连接舌头、耳朵与心。

normal.en: The cake was too sweet for her.
normal.cn: 这块蛋糕对她来说太甜了。

normal.en: She has a sweet voice.
He brought a bag of sweets.
Sweet dreams, little one.
The air was sweet with flowers.

abstract.en: Sweet is the first pleasure the tongue teaches us.
abstract.cn: 甜是舌头教给我们的第一种快乐。

abstract.en: A sweet voice can soften a hard message.
abstract.cn: 温柔的声音能软化严厉的消息。

abstract.en: What is sweet is not always what is good.
abstract.cn: 甜的并不总是好的。

examples.en: The cake was too sweet, so she ate only half.
examples.cn: 这块蛋糕太甜了，她只吃了一半。

examples.en: She has a sweet voice.
She gave the child a sweet.

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 古英语 swete（甜的）
dict_mnemonic.text: 古英语 swete 表示甜的，后来从味觉扩展到声音与性情，作名词时指糖果。

root: 来自古英语 swete，源于日耳曼语 swotja（甜的）。

sensesIntro.en: Sweet means sugary in taste, gentle and pleasant, or a piece of candy.
sensesIntro.cn: sweet 表示味甜、温柔悦人，或糖果。

core.en: Pleasure at the tip of the tongue spreading outward.
core.cn: 舌尖上的愉悦向外扩散。

branches.en: The cake was too sweet for her.
branches.cn: 这块蛋糕对她来说太甜了。

branches.en: The air was sweet with flowers.
branches.cn: 空气里满是花香。

branches.en: She has a sweet voice.
branches.cn: 她的嗓音很悦耳。

branches.en: She gave the child a sweet.
branches.cn: 她给了孩子一颗糖。

branches.en: Taste and manner can both be sweet.
branches.cn: 味道与举止都可以甜美。

intro.en: Sweet forms sweeter, sweetest, and the verb sweeten.
intro.cn: sweet 构成比较级、最高级以及动词 sweeten。

latinIntro.en: Sweet is Germanic; Latin dulcis, sweet, appears in dulcet.
latinIntro.cn: sweet 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 dulcis（甜的）见于 dulcet。

latinEntries.example: Latin dulcis means sweet.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 dulcis 意为甜的。

definition_zh: 游泳；游动；浸在液体中；眩晕
definition_en: to move through water using the body, or to seem to spin around
core_image: 孩子在水面划开双臂，身体贴着水线前进
scene: 夏天他们去河里游泳。In summer they swim in the river.
sceneCN: 这里 swim 是「游泳」（第 1 个义项）；句意：夏天他们去河里游泳。

senses.title: To move through water
senses.definition: to move through water by moving the arms and legs
senses.definitionCN: 靠划动四肢在水中前进
senses.example: In summer they swim in the river.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天他们去河里游泳。
senses.why: This is the physical action the word first named.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最早命名的身体动作。

senses.title: To be covered in liquid
senses.definition: to be covered with or full of liquid
senses.definitionCN: 被液体覆盖或充满
senses.example: The vegetables were swimming in oil.
senses.exampleCN: 蔬菜浸在油里。
senses.why: The image of moving in water is transferred to food sitting in sauce.
senses.whyCN: 在水中移动的画面被移用到泡在汤汁里的食物上。

senses.title: To feel dizzy
senses.definition: to seem to go round and round
senses.definitionCN: 感觉一切在旋转
senses.example: The room began to swim before his eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 房间开始在他眼前旋转。
senses.why: A swimmer loses steady footing, so the word also names the unstable feeling itself.
senses.whyCN: 游泳者失去稳定立足点，于是这个词也用来命名那种不稳的感觉。

senses.title: The activity of swimming
senses.definition: the act or sport of moving through water
senses.definitionCN: 在水中前进的活动或运动
senses.example: She had a long swim before breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 早饭前她游了很久。
senses.why: The verb became a noun for the whole activity, as English often does.
senses.whyCN: 动词转成名词，指整个活动，这在英语里很常见。

intro.en: Swim comes from an old Germanic verb for moving through water.
intro.cn: swim 源自古老的日耳曼语动词，意为在水中移动。

items.en: The Germanic root carried the idea of moving through water.
items.cn: 日耳曼语词根带有在水中行进的含义。

items.en: Swimman meant to swim.
Swimmen kept the water sense and added floating.
items.cn: swimmen 保留水中之义，并增添漂浮之义。

items.en: Swim also described things covered in liquid.
items.cn: swim 也用来描述浸在液体中的东西。

items.en: Swim gained the sense of a dizzy, spinning feeling.
items.cn: swim 又获得眩晕旋转之意。

note.en: Swim is compared with look-alike words and with other water verbs.
note.cn: 把 swim 与形近词以及其他水中动作词作比较。

entries.definition: to stay on the surface of water

normalIntro.en: Swim names the body pushing through water.
normalIntro.cn: swim 指身体在水中前进。

normal.en: In summer they swim in the river.
She learned to swim at the age of six.
The vegetables were swimming in oil.
The room began to swim before his eyes.
normal.cn: 房间开始在他眼前旋转。

normal.en: He had a long swim before breakfast.

abstract.en: To swim is to trust the water to hold you.
abstract.cn: 游泳就是相信水会托住你。

abstract.en: Swim also means to lose your footing in the world.
abstract.cn: swim 也指在世界中失去立足点。

abstract.en: A swim is a small journey with no road.
abstract.cn: 一次游泳是一段没有道路的小旅程。

examples.en: In summer they swim in the river.
She learned to swim at the age of six.
The vegetables were swimming in oil.

dict_mnemonic.note: 不规则变化 · swim - swam - swum
dict_mnemonic.text: swim 是不规则动词，过去式 swam，过去分词 swum；加 -mer 成为 swimmer，即游泳的人。

root: 来自古英语 swimman，源于日耳曼语，核心是在水中靠身体前进。

sensesIntro.en: Swim means to move through water, to lie in liquid, or to feel dizzy.
sensesIntro.cn: swim 表示在水中前进、浸在液体中，或感到眩晕。

core.en: A body pushing through a yielding element.
core.cn: 身体在柔软介质中前行。

branches.en: In summer they swim in the river.
branches.cn: 夏天他们去河里游泳。

branches.en: She learned to swim at the age of six.
branches.cn: 她六岁学会游泳。

branches.en: The vegetables were swimming in oil.
branches.cn: 蔬菜浸在油里。

branches.en: The room began to swim before his eyes.
branches.cn: 房间开始在他眼前旋转。

branches.en: He had a long swim before breakfast.
branches.cn: 早饭前他游了很久。

intro.en: Swim forms swims, swimming, swam, swum and the noun swimmer.
intro.cn: swim 可构成 swims、swimming、swam、swum 与名词 swimmer。

latinIntro.en: Swim is Germanic; Latin natare, to swim, gives natation.
latinIntro.cn: swim 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 natare（游泳）衍生出 natation。

items.example: She has swum for an hour.

latinEntries.example: Latin natare means to swim.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 natare 意为游泳。
